question_text: An infinitely long thin straight wire held perpendicular to the plane of the paper at point $O$ carries a current $I$ into the paper as shown in the figure. Nine other similar infinitely long wires, parallel to each consecutive wires is 30$^\circ$. Except for wire A and B, the direction of the magnetic force per unit length on the wire at the centre $O$ due to other wires. [Take cos 30$^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$]

options.option_text: $\frac{\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi r}(2+\sqrt{3})$ in the direction of YO.
$\frac{\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi r}(1+\sqrt{3})$ in the direction of OY.
$\frac{\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi r}(1+\sqrt{5})$ in the direction of OX.
$\frac{\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi r}(2+\sqrt{5})$ in the direction of OX.
$\frac{\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi r}(2-\sqrt{5})$ in the direction of YO.
